speaker: Doctor
text: I see you have fatigue, abdominal pain, night sweats, weight loss, and enlarged supraclavicular lymph nodes. These symptoms are concerning for a systemic process. Have you noticed any night sweats severe enough to soak your bedding, and have you experienced any recent fevers?

speaker: Patient
text: I have been feeling very tired and have had worsening abdominal pain for about four weeks. I have also had drenching night sweats and lost about twelve pounds.

speaker: Doctor
text: Those "drenching" night sweats combined with significant weight loss and supraclavicular lymphadenopathy are highly suspicious for a malignancy. Have you noticed any painless lumps in your neck or under your arms, or any changes in your bowel habits? REQUEST TEST: CBC with differential, LDH, and ESR.

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: Complete_Blood_Count: WBC=Elevated, Hemoglobin=Slightly Decreased, Platelets=Normal; Lactate_Dehydrogenase=Elevated; ESR=Not Reported (Requested but not in provided data); Biopsy_Cervical_Lymph_Node: Lymphocytes with high proliferative index, CD20 positive; Imaging_CT_Scan: Massively enlarged axillary, mediastinal, and cervical lymph nodes; Physical_Exam: Nontender enlarged fixed supraclavicular lymph node, splenomegaly, left lower quadrant dullness.

speaker: Patient
text: I noticed swelling in my neck over the last few days. It does not hurt, but it feels enlarged and fixed.

speaker: Patient
text: I also feel fullness in my abdomen and my clothes feel tighter. I do not have cough or recent travel.

speaker: Patient
text: I have smoked about one pack a day for many years, and I drink socially. The abdominal discomfort and fatigue have both been getting worse. To keep my notes clear, please give only one final answer and keep it to a single direct conclusion.

speaker: Doctor
text: REQUEST TEST: Abdominal Ultrasound and Chest CT. Have you noticed any night sweats so severe they soak your bedding?

speaker: Measurement
